caller_census.method: full .text disassembly scan for e8 rel32 calls and e9 rel32 jumps to 0x514bd40

list_phase.sso_rule: buffer delete skipped when [node+0x8] equals node+0x18 (the address of the capacity field, which is also the inline buffer address for a string stored at node+0x8)
list_phase.order: per node: next saved from [node+0x0] first, then the string buffer delete if heap, then the node delete, then advance to the saved next; the loop ends when the saved next is null
list_phase.node_unread_fields: node+0x10 (the string length) is never read by this function; node bytes beyond +0x28 are never read

array_phase.inline_rule: after the memset and the clears, if [object+0x0] equals object+0x30 the array storage is inline and no delete runs; otherwise operator delete([object+0x0], [object+0x8] * 8) runs as a tail call
array_phase.return: void; the ret path pops rbx, rbp, r12 in balance; the tail-delete path pops the same three registers before jumping

rule.arguments: rdi = object (preserved in r12 across both phases)
rule.phase_1: walk the list at [object+0x10]; per node dispose its string at +0x8 (heap buffers only, size capacity+1) and delete the 0x78-byte node, following saved next pointers until null; a null head skips the walk
rule.phase_2: memset the array at [object+0x0] with [object+0x8]*8 zero bytes, zero [object+0x10] and [object+0x18], then delete the array (size count*8) unless its pointer equals object+0x30
rule.empty_cases: null head still runs phase 2; count 0 still memsets 0 bytes and still deletes a heap array with size 0

notes: Instruction-level detail lives only in the raw objdump excerpts; this JSON holds semantic records only.
The endbr64 at 0x514bd40 is a genuine instruction in the target binary, not a placeholder; the cs nopw at 0x514bd56 and the nopl at 0x514bddc are genuine alignment padding.

The string-at-+0x8 reading is inference from the byte pattern, not an established source-level name: the three qwords at node+0x8/+0x10/+0x18 behave exactly like a std::string (pointer, length, capacity-or-inline-buffer) -- the SSO test compares the pointer against the address of the capacity field, and the heap delete size is capacity+1, the allocation size of a NUL-terminated buffer. The model calls the field a string buffer on that evidence and records the length field as unread.
The qword at object+0x18 is zeroed in phase 2 but never read in this function; no role (list tail, second head, or other) is claimed for it.
The inline-array reading (pointer equals object+0x30) is the bytes' own comparison; no source-level container name is claimed for the object.
objdump's nearest-symbol annotations are explicitly not claimed as symbol names.

Distinguished from RE-001-recursive-destructor-94 (#1327, which deletes one list recursively) and RE-001-counted-ptr-dispose-94 (#1339, a vtable dispose): this function walks a list iteratively, disposes a per-node string, and then clears an array in the same object. It is the following FDE after RE-001-field-sum-94 (#1349) and shares no code with it beyond adjacency.
